reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The results of a long jump competition were reported as follows:

| | Average Length |
| --- | --- |
| Team A | 3.6 m |
| Team B | 4.8 m |

There were the same number of students in each team.
Which statement about the competition MUST be true?

options.label: A
options.text: Each student in team B jumped farther than any student in team A.

options.label: B
options.text: After every student in team A jumped, there was a student in team B who jumped farther.

options.label: C
options.text: As a group, team B jumped farther than team A.

options.label: D
options.text: Some students in team A jumped farther than some students in team B.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Popularity of Subjects

A group of 10 students wanted to find out whether mathematics or history was more popular for their group. They rated each subject using the following scale.

[Image: Rating scale from 1 to 5]

The table shows the results:

Students’ Ratings

| Student | Mathematics Rating | History Rating |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alan | 1 | 2 |
| Lisa | 4 | 4 |
| Ann | 5 | 4 |
| John | 2 | 2 |
| Connor | 4 | 2 |
| Georgia | 3 | 3 |
| Bret | 2 | 1 |
| Courtney | 1 | 1 |
| Ian | 5 | 3 |
| Jackson | 3 | 2 |
| Totals | 30 | 24 |

A. Calculate the mean (average) rating for each subject.

Mean rating for mathematics = ____

Mean rating for history = ____

According to the ratings, which is the more popular subject for this group of students?

More popular subject: ____

descriptors:
3.0 or 3 for mathematics
2.4 for history
mathematics more popular
3.0 for mathematics OR 2.4 for history, not both.
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

- 1: "Dislike a lot"
- 2: "Dislike"
- 3: "Neither dislike nor like"
- 4: "Like"
- 5: "Like a lot"

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph represents the distance and time of a hike taken by Joshua and Liam.

[Image: Line graph of distance versus time]

If they both started from the same place and walked in the same direction, at what time did they meet?
reference_items.figure_description:
A line graph with a vertical axis labeled "Distance (kilometers)" marked from 0 to 5.5 in increments of 0.5 (labeled 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0, 5.5). The horizontal axis is labeled "Time" with tick marks every 30 minutes from 8:00 to 12:30 (labeled 8:00, 8:30, 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30). Two line segments are shown:
- One labeled "Joshua" begins at (8:00, 0) and ends with a solid dot at (12:00, 4.5).
- One labeled "Liam" begins at (9:00, 0) and ends with a solid dot at (11:00, 4.5).
The two lines intersect at time 10:00 and distance approximately 2.25 kilometers.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
